description: Money is represented with Python Decimal; float input is rejected and API serialization emits strings such as "1250.50".
steps: Construct Money from Decimal('1250.50') and serialize to JSON
Assert JSON value is the string '1250.50'
Assert constructing Money from float 12.5 raises a validation error

description: Money rejects negative values and more than 2 decimal places with distinct reason codes NEGATIVE_AMOUNT and OVER_PRECISION.
steps: Validate Decimal('-1') and Decimal('10.005') as payment amounts
Assert reason codes are NEGATIVE_AMOUNT and OVER_PRECISION respectively

description: Clock interface has a system implementation and a settable test/simulated implementation whose now() returns exactly the value set and advances by advance(days=n).
steps: Set TestClock to 2026-10-01
Call advance(days=3)
Assert now() equals 2026-10-04

description: Account.type accepts only CARD or PERSONAL_LOAN, and enums PTP status (PENDING, KEPT, BROKEN, CANCELLED) and intent labels (PAY_NOW, PROMISE_TO_PAY, PAYMENT_PLAN, FINANCIAL_HARDSHIP, DISPUTE, REQUEST_HUMAN, UNKNOWN) reject any other value.
steps: Instantiate Account with type 'MORTGAGE'
Assert validation error
Assert each listed enum value round-trips

description: EscalationReason accepts exactly REQUEST_HUMAN, UNRESOLVED_UNKNOWN, AI_FAILURE_FALLBACK, EXCEPTIONAL_ARRANGEMENT, FINANCIAL_HARDSHIP, DISPUTE, SETTLEMENT_REQUEST, AMBIGUOUS_VALIDATION, VULNERABLE_CUSTOMER, POLICY_EXCEPTION and HIGH_RISK_COMPLIANCE, the review queue and reviewer role enums reject any other value, and VULNERABLE_CUSTOMER is not an accepted intent label.
steps: Construct EscalationReason from each of the 11 valid values
Assert an unknown value such as SETTLEMENT_OFFER raises a validation error
Assert IntentLabel('VULNERABLE_CUSTOMER') raises a validation error

description: Loading the seeded rule set returns a version string (for example 'policy-v1') and every required parameter defined in specs/policy-ruleset-contract.md is present with the type, unit and range the contract specifies.
steps: Load the seeded rule set
Assert the version string is present
Assert every contract parameter exists and satisfies its type and range constraint

description: Rule set validation rejects a config with a missing required parameter, a wrong-typed or out-of-range value, negative weights or unordered band cut-offs, and the application fails to start with a named error identifying the parameter.
steps: Remove priority.band_cutoffs from a copy of the rule set and attempt startup
Assert startup fails with an error naming priority.band_cutoffs
Repeat with a negative weight and with cut-offs in descending order

description: With no valid active rule set at runtime every rules service returns POLICY_UNAVAILABLE and grants no eligibility, options or priority (fail closed).
steps: Deactivate the rule set in a test
Call the priority, PTP, arrangement and contact services
Assert each returns POLICY_UNAVAILABLE with no eligibility, options or score

description: Rule sets are immutable per version: changing any parameter creates a new version, exactly one version is active, and an earlier version referenced by an audit event can still be loaded read-only with its original values.
steps: Activate policy-v2 with a changed ptp.window_days
Assert policy-v1 still loads with its original ptp.window_days
Assert an attempt to update a parameter in place is rejected

description: The routing table maps every EscalationReason to exactly one queue and reviewer role as defined in the contract, and a table missing a reason or naming an unknown queue or role fails validation.
steps: Validate the seeded routing table against all 11 reasons
Remove DISPUTE from a copy and assert validation fails
Set an unknown queue name and assert validation fails

description: Configuration reads the model name from ANTHROPIC_MODEL and LIVE or MOCK mode from an environment variable, and no model id or secret is hard-coded in source.
steps: Grep source for 'claude-' literals and API key patterns outside tests and .env.example
Assert zero matches
Start with ANTHROPIC_MODEL=x and assert config.model == 'x'

description: Validated application configuration keys (tool call cap per turn, retry bound, maximum clarification turns, chat rate limit) are checked at startup against the contract ranges, the tool call cap defaults to 5, and a value of 0 or 21 fails startup with a named error.
steps: Start with no cap configured and assert the effective cap is 5
Start with cap 0 and assert a named startup error
Start with cap 21 and assert a named startup error

description: A .env file is git-ignored and .env.example lists required variables with placeholder values only.
steps: Run git check-ignore .env
Assert exit code 0
Assert .env.example contains no value matching an API key pattern

description: Seed script loads between 200 and 1,000 synthetic accounts including both CARD and PERSONAL_LOAN types and is idempotent when run twice.
steps: Run seed script
Assert account count between 200 and 1000 and both types present
Run seed again and assert count unchanged

description: Money columns are PostgreSQL NUMERIC and a round-trip of Decimal('0.10') through the repository returns Decimal('0.10') exactly.
steps: Inspect schema column types for NUMERIC
Save and reload an amount of 0.10
Assert equality with no float drift

description: Seed validation rejects inconsistent records (DPD not matching bucket, negative balance) and flags them with a reason instead of loading silently.
steps: Feed a record with DPD 95 and bucket 1-30
Assert it is rejected or flagged INCONSISTENT with reason
Assert negative balance record is rejected

description: Prohibited-pattern scan over seed data finds zero real-looking PII: emails only on example.com, phones only in the fictional range, no 13-19 digit card numbers, CVV, PIN or government ID patterns.
steps: Run the prohibited-pattern scanner on seed output
Assert exit code 0
Inject a 16-digit card number into a fixture and assert the scanner fails

description: The schema is created by versioned migrations that apply cleanly to an empty database and can be re-run without error.
steps: Run migrations on an empty PostgreSQL database
Assert all tables exist
Run migrations again and assert no error and no change

description: Every customer-owned record (account, conversation, PTP, PaymentEvent, arrangement, hardship case, dispute, escalation case) carries an owning customer_id foreign key, and a repository query by customer_id returns only that customer's records.
steps: Seed two customers with records of each type
Query each repository by the first customer_id
Assert none of the second customer's records are returned

description: DelinquencyRecord stores an as_of timestamp and a monotonically increasing version, and every update increments the version.
steps: Create a DelinquencyRecord and read version 1
Update the overdue amount
Assert version is 2 and as_of is advanced by the Clock

description: An AuditEvent contains timestamp from the injected Clock, account reference, capability, provider, model id, prompt version, PolicyRuleSet version, correlation id, provider latency, tool-call duration, end-to-end interaction duration, token usage where available, redacted input reference, AI output, tool calls, rule results, human override and final action fields.
steps: Write an audit event from a MOCK interaction with scripted latency 120 ms and 300 tokens
Read it back
Assert every listed field is present and the latency and token values match

description: The application database role cannot UPDATE or DELETE audit rows: attempted UPDATE and DELETE raise a permission error.
steps: Connect as the app role
Execute UPDATE and DELETE on audit_events
Assert both fail with permission denied

description: When the audit insert fails, the accompanying state transition is rolled back and no transition row persists.
steps: Force the audit insert to raise inside a transition
Assert the transition raises
Assert the entity state is unchanged in the database

description: Secrets and prohibited identifiers are redacted before an audit event is stored: an input containing an API key pattern is stored as [REDACTED].
steps: Write an event whose input includes 'sk-ant-abc123'
Read stored event
Assert stored text has [REDACTED] and not the key

description: When audit persistence fails for a non-state-changing activity the audit service raises AuditUnavailable, callers cannot report the activity as audited, and an operational failure log entry without customer data is written where possible.
steps: Force the audit insert to fail during a recommendation
Assert AuditUnavailable is raised to the caller
Assert an operational failure log line exists and contains no customer data

description: A README documents local startup and one documented command starts PostgreSQL, the API and the web app with Docker Compose from a clean checkout.
steps: Follow the README on a clean checkout
Run the documented start command
Assert the API health endpoint and the web app respond

description: A documented command applies migrations and loads the synthetic seed data, and the API reports ready afterwards.
steps: Run the migrate-and-seed command
Assert the account count is between 200 and 1,000
Assert the readiness endpoint returns ready

description: MOCK mode is the default and the full backend and frontend test suites run locally with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set and no network calls to the provider.
steps: Unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and start the test suites
Assert all suites run to completion
Assert a socket-blocking guard records zero outbound provider calls

description: A basic CI workflow runs backend, frontend and MOCK evaluation tests on every push, fails on any test failure, and excludes LIVE evaluation.
steps: Inspect the CI workflow file
Assert it runs backend, frontend and MOCK eval jobs
Assert LIVE evaluation is not executed and a failing test fails the workflow

description: No production deployment configuration is included: only local Compose files and the CI workflow exist.
steps: List deployment-related files in the repository
Assert there is no production manifest, cloud template or release pipeline

description: Given fixed inputs and policy-v1 the service returns the same score, band and ordered factor list on 100 repeated calls.
steps: Call priority service 100 times with fixed input
Assert all results are identical

description: Each returned factor names the input attribute, its value and its weighted contribution, and the contributions sum to the score.
steps: Compute priority for a sample account
Assert factors list has one entry per contributing input
Assert sum of contributions equals score

description: Band thresholds from the rule set map scores at each boundary (just below and at cut-off) to the expected band.
steps: Compute scores at cut-off-0.01 and cut-off for each threshold
Assert bands are LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL as configured

description: Accounts with an active dispute, active hardship case or open escalation return human_treatment=true and automated_treatment_suppressed=true.
steps: Compute priority for accounts with each condition
Assert both flags true
Assert flags false for a clean account

description: The rules engine package imports nothing from AI orchestration or LLM provider modules (checked by an architecture test).
steps: Run import-graph test on rules_engine
Assert no dependency on ai_orchestration or llm_provider

description: Priority parameters are read from the active PolicyRuleSet, and a missing or invalid parameter returns POLICY_UNAVAILABLE with no score produced.
steps: Provide a rule set with priority.weights.dpd missing
Call the priority service
Assert POLICY_UNAVAILABLE is returned and no score or band is present

description: Amounts of zero, negative, over the overdue balance and with more than 2 decimals are rejected with reason codes ZERO_AMOUNT, NEGATIVE_AMOUNT, OVER_BALANCE and OVER_PRECISION.
steps: Validate each of 0, -5, balance+0.01, 10.001
Assert corresponding reason code and no exception thrown

description: Dates in the past, and dates beyond the policy window (ptp_window_days from Clock now), are rejected with PAST_DATE and OUTSIDE_WINDOW; a date on the last permitted day is accepted.
steps: Set TestClock
Validate yesterday, last permitted day, last permitted day + 1
Assert PAST_DATE, accepted, OUTSIDE_WINDOW

description: A rejection response includes at least one valid alternative amount or date range computed by the service.
steps: Validate an over-balance amount
Assert alternatives contains the maximum permitted amount as a Decimal string

description: The payable-amounts function returns the overdue amount and the full outstanding balance as Decimal strings for an account and returns none for an account under suppression.
steps: Call payable options for a normal account
Assert two options with expected values
Call for a suppressed account and assert an empty list with reason SUPPRESSED

description: The PTP satisfaction rule sums only successful simulated PaymentEvents at or above the qualifying minimum that occur on or before the due date and returns KEPT when the cumulative total is at least the promised amount, PENDING before the deadline otherwise, and BROKEN after the deadline.
steps: Create a PTP for 300.00 due 2026-10-10 and payments totalling 300.00 on 2026-10-08
Assert the rule returns KEPT
Evaluate the same PTP with 100.00 paid and Clock at 2026-10-11 and assert BROKEN

description: A single qualifying payment below the promised amount returns PENDING with cumulative_paid and remaining amounts as Decimal strings, and a second payment that brings the total to the promised amount returns KEPT.
steps: Apply a payment of 100.00 to a 300.00 PTP
Assert PENDING with cumulative_paid '100.00' and remaining '200.00'
Apply a second payment of 200.00 and assert KEPT

description: FAILED PaymentEvents, payments below the qualifying minimum and payments dated after the due date are excluded from the cumulative total.
steps: Add a FAILED payment, a payment below ptp.qualifying_payment_min_amount and a late payment
Evaluate the PTP
Assert cumulative_paid excludes all three

description: For a fixed account and policy-v1 the service returns a stable list of options whose installments sum exactly to the arranged amount (no rounding loss).
steps: Request options for a 1000.00 overdue account
Assert each option's installments sum to the arranged total with Decimal equality

description: An account that fails eligibility (for example already has an active arrangement or DPD beyond the limit) returns an empty option list with a reason code.
steps: Request options for an ineligible account
Assert options == [] and reason code present

description: A requested term or date outside permitted ranges is classified EXCEPTIONAL and one inside is classified ELIGIBLE.
steps: Classify a request with term max+1
Assert EXCEPTIONAL
Classify a request within range and assert ELIGIBLE

description: A conflicting active PTP or arrangement blocks a new arrangement with reason CONFLICTING_ACTIVE_ITEM and lists amend or cancel as the permitted path.
steps: Create active PTP fixture
Request options
Assert blocked with CONFLICTING_ACTIVE_ITEM

description: If the rules engine raises an internal error the service returns a failure result (no options, no guess) and records the rule-set version.
steps: Inject a rule loader failure
Assert result status is RULES_ERROR with no options
Assert rule-set version present

description: Contact is denied with reason MAX_ATTEMPTS when attempts in the period reach the configured maximum and allowed when one below.
steps: Set attempts to max-1 and call can_contact
Assert allowed
Set attempts to max and assert denied MAX_ATTEMPTS

description: Contact is denied with reason MIN_INTERVAL when the last attempt is within the configured interval under the TestClock and allowed after it.
steps: Record an attempt
Advance clock to interval-1h and assert denied
Advance to interval and assert allowed

description: An active dispute on an item suppresses automated recommendations for that item only, while other items on the account remain eligible.
steps: Create account with two items and a dispute on one
Assert item A suppressed and item B not

description: Active hardship or a vulnerable-customer flag suppresses all automated treatment for the account until cleared by a human decision.
steps: Set hardship flag
Assert suppression true
Record human decision clearing it and assert suppression false

description: The freshness check compares a snapshot's as_of and version to the current record and the freshness threshold and returns FRESH, STALE or UNKNOWN.
steps: Check a snapshot younger than the threshold with the current version
Assert FRESH
Check an older snapshot and a snapshot with a missing as_of and assert STALE and UNKNOWN

description: A stale snapshot or a version mismatch causes the consequential action to be refused with reason STALE_DATA and the refreshed context to be returned.
steps: Change the record version after a proposal is built
Attempt the consequential action
Assert STALE_DATA, no state change and refreshed context returned

description: When freshness cannot be established (UNKNOWN) the action fails closed with no state change and is reported for escalation with reason AMBIGUOUS_VALIDATION.
steps: Remove as_of from a snapshot
Attempt a PTP creation
Assert no PTP, an AMBIGUOUS_VALIDATION escalation request and an audit event

description: The rules engine refuses internally inconsistent records (DPD not matching bucket, negative balance, overdue amount above outstanding balance) with reason INCONSISTENT_RECORD and flags the record.
steps: Evaluate a record with DPD 95 and bucket 1-29
Assert INCONSISTENT_RECORD and the record flagged
Repeat with a negative balance and overdue above outstanding

description: Every rules service invoked with an inconsistent or unfresh record returns a failure result and never an eligibility, option or score.
steps: Call priority, PTP, payable-amount and arrangement services with an inconsistent record
Assert each returns a failure result
Assert no option list or score is present

description: For each of the 11 EscalationReason values the routing service returns the contract queue and reviewer role: REQUEST_HUMAN, UNRESOLVED_UNKNOWN, AI_FAILURE_FALLBACK, SETTLEMENT_REQUEST and AMBIGUOUS_VALIDATION to COLLECTIONS_REVIEW and COLLECTIONS_OFFICER; EXCEPTIONAL_ARRANGEMENT to COLLECTIONS_EXCEPTION_REVIEW and COLLECTIONS_OFFICER; FINANCIAL_HARDSHIP to HARDSHIP_REVIEW and COLLECTIONS_OFFICER; DISPUTE to DISPUTE_REVIEW and COLLECTIONS_OFFICER; VULNERABLE_CUSTOMER to VULNERABLE_CUSTOMER_REVIEW and COLLECTIONS_OFFICER; POLICY_EXCEPTION and HIGH_RISK_COMPLIANCE to COMPLIANCE_REVIEW and COMPLIANCE_RISK.
steps: Run a parametrized test over all 11 reasons
Assert each returns the mapped queue and reviewer role
Assert exactly COMPLIANCE_RISK is returned only for POLICY_EXCEPTION and HIGH_RISK_COMPLIANCE

description: An unrecognized or missing reason fails closed to COLLECTIONS_REVIEW and COLLECTIONS_OFFICER and the result is flagged reason_unrecognized.
steps: Call the routing service with 'BANK_MANAGER_ESCALATION' and with None
Assert COLLECTIONS_REVIEW and COLLECTIONS_OFFICER for both
Assert reason_unrecognized is true

description: The routing function accepts only the reason and case context and never a queue or reviewer role argument, and its result contains reason, queue, reviewer role, priority and the PolicyRuleSet version used.
steps: Inspect the routing function signature
Assert passing queue or reviewer_role raises an error
Assert the result includes reason, queue, reviewer_role, priority and rule_set_version

description: VULNERABLE_CUSTOMER and FINANCIAL_HARDSHIP cases receive at least the ELEVATED priority defined by the routing priority parameters, and identical inputs always return the identical priority.
steps: Route a VULNERABLE_CUSTOMER and a FINANCIAL_HARDSHIP case
Assert priority is ELEVATED or URGENT per the rule set
Repeat 50 times and assert identical results

description: If the active rule set is unavailable the routing service returns the COLLECTIONS_REVIEW fallback with POLICY_UNAVAILABLE recorded and never an empty routing.
steps: Deactivate the rule set
Route a DISPUTE reason
Assert COLLECTIONS_REVIEW, COLLECTIONS_OFFICER and POLICY_UNAVAILABLE recorded

description: A request without a persona header returns 401 and a request from a role not allowed on an endpoint returns 403 with body code FORBIDDEN.
steps: Call GET /api/portfolio with no persona
Assert 401
Call with persona CUSTOMER
Assert 403

description: Every 403 produces an audit event containing persona, endpoint and correlation id.
steps: Trigger a 403
Query audit events
Assert one event with the persona, endpoint and correlation id

description: A generated role x endpoint matrix test covers every registered route for all four personas and asserts the documented allow or deny outcome.
steps: Enumerate routes from the app
For each persona x route assert status matches the permission table
Assert failure if a route lacks a table entry

description: COLLECTIONS_MANAGER receives 403 on every mutating endpoint (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), and COMPLIANCE_RISK receives 403 on every mutating endpoint except the record_compliance_review_decision endpoint.
steps: Enumerate all mutating routes from the route registry
Call each as COLLECTIONS_MANAGER and assert 403
Call each as COMPLIANCE_RISK and assert 403 except the compliance decision route

description: The record_compliance_review_decision capability is allowed only for COMPLIANCE_RISK and returns 403 for CUSTOMER, COLLECTIONS_OFFICER and COLLECTIONS_MANAGER, and COMPLIANCE_RISK holds no other mutating capability.
steps: Call the compliance decision endpoint as each of the four personas
Assert only COMPLIANCE_RISK is allowed
Assert COMPLIANCE_RISK receives 403 on all other mutating routes

description: GET /api/portfolio returns items with customer name, account type, outstanding balance, overdue amount, DPD, bucket, collection status and priority band for each account.
steps: Call GET /api/portfolio as COLLECTIONS_OFFICER
Assert 200
Assert each item contains all listed fields and money values are strings

description: Filtering by dpd_min, dpd_max, priority_band and status returns only matching accounts and combined filters intersect.
steps: Call with priority_band=HIGH
Assert all items HIGH
Add dpd_min=60 and assert all items also have DPD >= 60

description: Sorting by overdue amount and DPD ascending and descending returns correctly ordered results using Decimal comparison.
steps: Call with sort=overdue&order=desc
Assert non-increasing Decimal order
Repeat for dpd asc

description: The portfolio endpoint is allowed only for COLLECTIONS_OFFICER and returns 403 for CUSTOMER, COLLECTIONS_MANAGER and COMPLIANCE_RISK.
steps: Call GET /api/portfolio as each persona
Assert COLLECTIONS_OFFICER receives 200
Assert the other three receive 403

description: The table renders columns customer, product type, balance, overdue, DPD, bucket, status and priority band, and the band shows a text label as well as color.
steps: Open /portfolio as officer
Assert column headers
Assert a band cell contains text such as 'High' and not only a color

description: Selecting DPD, priority band and status filters updates the rows shown and the URL query, and clearing filters restores the full list.
steps: Select priority band High
Assert all rows show High
Click clear and assert row count returns to default

description: Clicking the overdue and DPD column headers sorts the table and sets aria-sort accordingly.
steps: Click Overdue header
Assert first two rows are in descending overdue order
Assert aria-sort attribute set

description: Clicking a row navigates to /customers/{accountId} (Customer 360) and the table passes an axe scan with zero serious or critical violations and is operable by keyboard.
steps: Focus a row link with Tab and press Enter
Assert URL matches /customers/
Run axe on /portfolio and assert 0 serious or critical

description: Portfolio main content is interactive in under 2 s p95 over 30 scripted Playwright loads after one warm-up on the 1,000-account dataset.
steps: Load /portfolio 31 times
Discard the first
Assert p95 interactive < 2000 ms and log hardware

description: The switcher lists exactly CUSTOMER, COLLECTIONS_OFFICER, COLLECTIONS_MANAGER and COMPLIANCE_RISK, selecting one sends that persona on subsequent API calls, and selecting CUSTOMER requires choosing one seeded demo customer whose id is bound server-side.
steps: Open the switcher and list the options
Select CUSTOMER and choose a seeded demo customer
Assert subsequent API calls carry the persona and the server binds the chosen customer_id

description: Navigation shows only permitted links per persona: CUSTOMER sees Chat only, COLLECTIONS_OFFICER sees Portfolio, Customer 360 and the escalation queues, COLLECTIONS_MANAGER sees the Dashboard only, and COMPLIANCE_RISK sees the Audit Trail and the compliance review queue.
steps: Switch to each persona in turn
Read the visible navigation links
Assert the links match the persona's permitted set exactly

description: Navigating directly to a route the persona cannot access shows a forbidden page and does not render restricted data.
steps: As CUSTOMER open /portfolio
Assert forbidden message
Assert no account data in the DOM

description: The shell shows a visible 'Demo persona - not real authentication' label and the current persona name as text.
steps: Load app
Assert label text present
Assert current persona name displayed

description: The persona switcher and navigation are operable by keyboard alone with a visible focus indicator, and the current persona is announced to assistive technology.
steps: Tab to the switcher and change persona using the keyboard only
Assert a visible focus indicator on each control
Assert the current persona is exposed via an accessible name or live region

description: The CUSTOMER persona is bound server-side to exactly one synthetic customer_id, and a client-supplied customer_id in a request is ignored or rejected.
steps: Select the CUSTOMER persona for customer A
Send a request that includes customer B's id in the body and query
Assert the server uses customer A's bound id and never customer B's

description: For every customer-facing request the server validates the persona, the bound customer_id and ownership of the requested resource, covering accounts, conversations, PTPs, PaymentEvents, arrangements, hardship records, disputes and escalation cases.
steps: Enumerate the customer-facing routes for each resource type
Request each resource owned by the bound customer and assert success
Request each resource owned by another customer and assert it is denied

description: A cross-customer request returns the same not-found response as a nonexistent resource, with no resource information leaked in the body or headers.
steps: Request another customer's account id and a nonexistent id
Compare status code, body and headers
Assert they are identical and contain no resource details

description: An authorization test matrix runs every customer-owned resource type against own, other-customer and nonexistent ids and passes for all cells.
steps: Generate the matrix over resource types x (own, other, nonexistent)
Run all cells
Assert expected allow or not-found outcomes for every cell

description: A denied cross-customer access writes an audit event with persona, bound customer_id and endpoint but not the target resource's contents.
steps: Trigger a cross-customer request
Read the audit event
Assert persona, bound customer id and endpoint are present and the target resource contents are absent

description: GET /api/customers/{accountId}/360 returns profile, account, outstanding balance, overdue amount, DPD, bucket, interactions, PTP history, hardship indicators, disputes and escalation status.
steps: Call as COLLECTIONS_OFFICER for a seeded account
Assert 200
Assert each listed section key present

description: The payload places priority band and contributing factors under a source='deterministic' block and any recommendation under source='ai' with model id and prompt version.
steps: Call the endpoint
Assert priority.source == 'deterministic'
Assert recommendation.source == 'ai' with model and prompt_version

description: An unknown account id returns 404 and CUSTOMER persona receives 403.
steps: GET with random id as officer, assert 404
GET as CUSTOMER, assert 403

description: Customer 360 is allowed only for COLLECTIONS_OFFICER and returns 403 for COLLECTIONS_MANAGER and COMPLIANCE_RISK.
steps: Call GET /api/customers/{accountId}/360 as each persona
Assert COLLECTIONS_OFFICER receives 200
Assert COLLECTIONS_MANAGER and COMPLIANCE_RISK receive 403

description: The payload includes the snapshot as_of timestamp, record version and a freshness state of FRESH, STALE or UNKNOWN from the freshness service.
steps: Request Customer 360 for a fresh account and a stale account
Assert as_of and version are present
Assert freshness is FRESH and STALE respectively

description: The screen shows DPD, bucket, overdue amount, priority band with each contributing factor, active PTP or arrangement and recent interactions.
steps: Open /customers/{id}
Assert each labelled value is visible and factors list rendered

description: AI-generated content is inside a panel with the text label 'AI-generated' and deterministic data panels carry the label 'Rules engine', with the distinction conveyed by text and icon and not color alone.
steps: Open Customer 360
Assert both labels present
Assert labels are text nodes

description: Escalation status, hardship indicators and dispute status are visible and an account with an OPEN escalation shows the badge 'Escalated - human review'.
steps: Open an account with open escalation
Assert badge text and status sections

description: Simulated payments in the history are labelled 'Simulated' and the page passes axe with zero serious or critical violations.
steps: Open an account with a PaymentEvent
Assert 'Simulated' label
Run axe and assert 0 serious or critical

description: Customer 360 main content is interactive in under 2 s p95 over 30 scripted loads after one warm-up.
steps: Load the page 31 times
Discard the first
Assert p95 < 2000 ms

description: When the AI provider is unavailable the screen shows an 'AI unavailable - manual workflow available' state, fabricates no recommendation, and all deterministic data and manual actions remain usable; a STALE or UNKNOWN snapshot shows a stale-data banner with a refresh action.
steps: Script the MOCK provider to time out and load Customer 360
Assert the AI unavailable banner is shown and no recommendation text is rendered
Assert deterministic panels and the manual Record Promise form remain usable and the stale banner appears for a stale snapshot

description: Keyboard navigation reaches every panel and control on the screen, and any dialog moves focus in on open, traps focus while open and returns focus to its trigger on close.
steps: Tab through the page using the keyboard only
Open the Record Promise dialog and assert focus moves into it and is trapped
Close it and assert focus returns to the trigger

description: A Record Promise-to-Pay form lets the officer record a customer commitment manually and works when the AI provider is unavailable.
steps: Open the form as COLLECTIONS_OFFICER with the MOCK provider timing out
Submit a valid amount and date
Assert the PTP appears as PENDING in the history

description: The recommendation output validates against a schema with action (one of the allowed actions), rationale text and referenced factor ids, and a schema-invalid MOCK output triggers one retry then a safe 'human review' recommendation.
steps: Run NBA with valid MOCK output and assert schema-valid result
Run with invalid output twice and assert action == ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN_REVIEW

description: The rationale is rejected and replaced by templated text if it cites a factor, amount or option not returned by the deterministic services.
steps: MOCK returns rationale citing amount 999.99 not in context
Assert final rationale equals the templated fallback
Assert a grounding-block audit event

description: For an account with active dispute, hardship or open escalation the only action returned is ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN_REVIEW regardless of AI output.
steps: Set active dispute
MOCK returns REQUEST_PAYMENT
Assert returned action is ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN_REVIEW

description: Each recommendation creates an audit event with model id, prompt version, rule-set version and output, and no financial record changes during generation.
steps: Generate recommendation
Assert audit event fields
Assert account balances and PTP rows unchanged

description: If audit persistence fails the recommendation endpoint returns an AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE state with no recommendation body, so the recommendation is never presented as governed.
steps: Force the audit insert to fail
Request a recommendation
Assert the response is AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE with no action or rationale and an operational failure is logged

description: Mode is chosen by configuration and MOCK makes zero network calls (verified by a test that blocks sockets).
steps: Set mode MOCK and block outbound sockets
Invoke provider
Assert scripted response returned without error

description: The MOCK provider can be scripted to return valid, malformed, adversarial and timeout responses per test case.
steps: Script each of four behaviors
Assert the provider returns or raises accordingly

description: Provider results include model id, latency in ms and token usage where available, and timeouts raise ProviderTimeout after the configured limit.
steps: Invoke provider with a scripted 2 s delay and 1 s timeout
